chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from al-Ḥasan, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

If you miss the witr of your night, then whenever you make it up on the following day before midday, you make it up as witr; and whenever you make it up at night, you make it up as witr; and whenever you make it up in the daytime after that day, you make it up as an even-numbered prayer, adding another rakʿah to it so that it becomes even.
He said: I said to him, 'And why was it made even?' He said: 'As a punishment for his neglect of the witr.'
As for that which indicates that when he prays sitting, it is permissible for him to perform one rakʿah by one rakʿah.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday, the point after which the sun declines from its zenith
key_terms.تَضْيِيعِهِ: his neglecting or wasting of the prayer
key_terms.تُضِيفُ: you add, meaning an additional rakʿah is joined to the prayer
key_terms.جَالِسًا: while sitting, referring to the posture of prayer
key_terms.شَفْعًا: an even-numbered prayer formed by adding another rakʿah
key_terms.عُقُوبَةً: as a penalty or consequence for neglect
key_terms.وِتْرًا: the odd-numbered witr prayer performed as a single rakʿah

ai.seo_question: How should a missed witr prayer be made up according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal method of making up a missed witr prayer depending on when it is performed. If it is made up before midday of the next day or at night, it remains witr, but if it is made up in the daytime after that day, it is performed as an even-numbered prayer by adding another rakʿah. The narration also states that this change to shafʿ is a consequence for having neglected the original witr.
